knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)

```{r}
library(simcompR)
```

A compiled plan can be run many times with different parameters. Model
parameters are declared in `sim_model(params = )` and referenced from
blocks with `sim_param()`.

## A second-order system

$G(s) = \frac{\omega^2}{s^2 + 2\zeta\omega s + \omega^2}$ with $\omega = 2$ and a
unit step input. Parameters can be any R value, including vectors, so the
whole denominator is one parameter:

```{r}
second <- sim_model("second_order", params = list(den = c(1, 0.8, 4), num = 4))
sim_add_block(second, "step", "u", time = 0)
sim_add_block(second, "transfer_function", "G",
              num = sim_param("num"), den = sim_param("den"))
sim_connect(second, "u", "G")
plan <- sim_compile(second)
```

Parameters can be combined where they are used. Writing the system with
$\zeta$ and $\omega$ as parameters keeps the denominator in its textbook
form; the expression is evaluated again for every run:

```{r}
named <- sim_model("second_order_zw", params = list(zeta = 0.2, w = 2))
sim_add_block(named, "step", "u", time = 0)
sim_add_block(named, "transfer_function", "G",
              num = sim_param("w")^2,
              den = sim_param_expr("c(1, 2 * zeta * w, w^2)"))
sim_connect(named, "u", "G")
zw <- sim_compile(named)
peak_of <- function(p) max(sim_signal(sim_run(p, c(0, 15), times = seq(0, 15, 0.01)), "G"))
c(zeta_0.2 = peak_of(zw), zeta_0.5 = peak_of(sim_set_params(zw, zeta = 0.5)))
```

Model parameters are also visible by name inside `expression` blocks and
state machine guards and actions.

## Sweeps

`sim_sweep()` takes a data frame with one row per run, or a list of named
lists for vector-valued parameters. `summary` reduces each result to named
numbers.

```{r}
dens <- lapply(c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 1), function(z) list(den = c(1, 2 * z * 2, 4)))
peak <- function(r) {
  y <- sim_signal(r, "G")
  t <- sim_times(r)
  outside <- which(abs(y - 1) > 0.02)
  c(peak = max(y), settle = if (length(outside)) t[max(outside)] else 0)
}
s <- sim_sweep(plan, dens, tspan = c(0, 15), times = seq(0, 15, 0.01), summary = peak)
s
cbind(zeta = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 1), s$summary[c("peak", "settle")],
      exact_peak = c(1 + exp(-pi * c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7) / sqrt(1 - c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7)^2)), 1))
```

The overshoot matches the classical formula $1 + e^{-\pi\zeta/\sqrt{1-\zeta^2}}$.

`s$parameters` records the value each parameter actually had in each run,
including model values a run did not override. Scalars that share a type
and class form an ordinary column (a `Date` stays a `Date`); vector
values, like the denominators here, form a list column:

```{r}
s$parameters$den[[2]]
```

```{r}
cols <- seq_along(s$results)
matplot(sim_times(s$results[[1]]), sapply(s$results, sim_signal, "G"),
        type = "l", lty = 1, col = cols, xlab = "time", ylab = "G")
legend("topright", paste("zeta =", c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 1)), col = cols, lty = 1)
```

### Reuse of the compiled structure

Each run calls `sim_set_params()`. When a new value keeps sizes,
feedthrough, state dimensions and sample times, the graph analysis is
reused; otherwise it is redone. Changing the order of the denominator above
would change the number of states and trigger a fresh analysis
automatically.

## Monte Carlo

`sim_monte_carlo()` draws parameter sets under a fixed seed. The caller's
random stream (`.Random.seed` and `RNGkind()`) is saved and restored, so
the experiment is reproducible and does not disturb other random code,
including when the sampler fails. With `keep = FALSE` only the summaries
are kept, which saves memory for many runs:

```{r}
set.seed(2024)
before <- runif(1)
set.seed(2024)
mc <- sim_monte_carlo(plan, n = 50,
  sampler = function(i) list(den = c(1, 2 * runif(1, 0.1, 0.9) * 2, 4)),
  seed = 1, tspan = c(0, 15), times = seq(0, 15, 0.05), keep = FALSE,
  summary = function(r) c(peak = max(sim_signal(r, "G"))))
after <- runif(1)
identical(before, after)
summary(mc$summary$peak)
hist(mc$summary$peak, main = "Peak response", xlab = "peak")
```

Running it again with the same seed returns identical numbers.

One restriction: with `RNGkind(normal.kind = "Box-Muller")`, R keeps the
second deviate of each Box-Muller pair outside `.Random.seed`, and that
cached value cannot be restored from R. `sim_monte_carlo()` warns in that
case, and the caller's next `rnorm()` may differ from what it would have
been. With the default `"Inversion"` (and the other normal kinds) the
stream is restored exactly.

## Noise inputs

`white_noise` blocks draw a value at each sample hit from their own seed,
the hit index and the element index, with a counter-based generator that
never touches R's random number generator. Results are reproducible, do
not depend on the global random state and leave it untouched:

```{r}
nm <- sim_model("noisy")
sim_add_block(nm, "white_noise", "w", sd = 0.2, period = 0.05, seed = 3)
sim_add_block(nm, "transfer_function", "filter", num = 1, den = c(0.5, 1))
sim_connect(nm, "w", "filter")
r1 <- sim_run(sim_compile(nm), c(0, 5))
r2 <- sim_run(sim_compile(nm), c(0, 5))
identical(r1$signals, r2$signals)
plot(r1, c("w", "filter"))
```

## Failures inside experiments

Runs that fail are kept with status `"failed"` and missing summaries; they
are never silently dropped. Each run uses `on_failure = "warn"` unless
another value is passed through `...`. Use `s$status` and `s$messages` to
inspect them:

```{r}
bad <- suppressWarnings(sim_sweep(plan, list(list(den = c(1, 1, 4)), list(den = c(1, 1, NA))),
                                  tspan = c(0, 1), times = c(0, 1)))
bad$status
bad$messages[2]
```

## Parallel runs

`cores > 1` runs simulations with `parallel::mclapply()` on Unix-like
systems; on Windows the runs are sequential. Results do not depend on the
number of cores, because every run is deterministic and seeds are drawn
before the runs start.
